COMMON JUDGMENT

Both the appeals arising out of the Common Award dated 29.01.2020 in M.C.O.P.Nos.115 & 116 of 2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sub Judge, Omalur, Salem District and both the appeals were filed by the Insurance Company, challenging the liability to pay the compensation on the ground that the deceased persons are travelled as an unauthorized passengers in the goods vehicle. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to hereunder according to their litigative status and ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The case of the claimants are that on 13.06.2014, at about 3.30 a.m., early hours, the deceased namely Rajendran - D1 and Shanmugam - D2 were returning after delivery of milk cans in Ashok Leyland minivan bearing Registration No.TN 30 AW 8815, while, they reached near Sanisanthai on Dharmapuri  Salem Main Road, the driver of the mini van drove it negligently and dashed on the rear side of the lorry bearing Registration No.TN 52 D 6748, which resulted in causing severe injuries to all the persons who travelled in the minivan.
Subsequently, they succumbed to their injuries.

4. Both the deceased were coolies used to travel in the minivan to deliver milk and after delivering,
they collected the milk cans and returned back to the office as per the instructions of the driver of the minivan.
They were earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month as a daily wage.

For the death of the deceased No.1 Rajendran, the dependents who are his wife, two children and his mother came forward with the Claim Petition seeking https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
17/03/2025 02:14:50 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.959 & 960 of 2022 compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

For the deceased No.2-Shanmugham, the dependents, who are his wife, son and father have filed this Claim Petition claiming compensation for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: The first respondent - owner of the minivan has not contested the claim and was remained ex-parte.

The second respondent -Insurance company of the minivan contested the claim, filed counter and contended that the deceased Rajendran and Shanmugham are not working as daily wagers and they were travelled in the minivan as an unauthorized passengers.
The lorry bearing registration No.TN 30 AW 8815 was stopped in the middle of the road, which resulted in causing the accident.
Hence, the owner of the lorry and Insurance Company is necessary parties in this Claim Petition and prays to dismiss the same.

5. After considering the evidences placed on record by both sides, the Tribunal has held that the deceased were not travelled as an unauthorized passengers and they were travelled as coolies for loading and unloading the milk cans.

Further, the Tribunal has held that the driver of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 17/03/2025 02:14:50 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.959 & 960 of 2022 mini van has negligently driven the vehicle and caused the accident thereby, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
It is also held that there is also a coverage for the coolies / daily wagers, accordingly, they are entitled for compensation and directed the respondents to pay the compensation.
6. Aggrieved over the liability fixed on the Insurance Company to pay the compensation, the present appeals have been filed by the Insurance Company.
The claimants have not filed any appeal or cross objection in this matter.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants submits that there is evidence placed on record, to show that the driver of the mini van has dashed on the rear side of the lorry since, the lorry was suddenly stopped in the middle of the road.
Hence, the negligence shall be fixed only on the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.TN 52 D 6748, since he had parked the vehicle negligently in the middle of the road.

She further submitted that there is also no evidence placed on record to show that the d e c e a s e d w e r e n o t w o r k i n g a s d a i l y w a g e r s a n d t h e y w e r e w o r k i n g i n a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 17/03/2025 02:14:50 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.959 & 960 of 2022 Coconut Farm and both the deceased were travelled as an unauthorized passengers.
These evidences were not properly appreciated by the Tribunal and prays to absolve the Insurance Company from indemnifying the respondent No.1 and prays to allow the appeal.

8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the claimants submitted that there is evidence placed on record shows that both the deceased were travelled only as load men i.e., to load and unload the milk cans.

The Trial Court has specifically recorded that in the vehicle milk cans were transported at the time of accident and though there was a slip answer given by one of the witness to the effect that the deceased were returning in the vehicle at the time of accident.
It does not convey any meaning to the effect that there is admission on the part of the claimants that the deceased were travelled as an unauthorized passengers.
Further, he would submit that there is insurance coverage for the deceased coolies and thereby, the insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle.
9. I have considered the submissions made on both sides and also perused the records.

sentences.text: On behalf of the claimants, the first claimants in both M.C.O.Ps were examined as witnesses and according to them, the deceased were involved in loading and unloading the milk cans, on the request of the driver of the minivan.

Accordingly, they went to deliver the milk and while returning,
after collecting the milk cans, the accident had taken place.
According to them, deceased were engaged for loading and unloading all the milk cans.

11. I have also perused the evidence adduced by them in the cross examination in which, there is not even a suggestion by the insurance company to show that the deceased were not engaged for loading and unloading activities.
The only defence in the entire cross examination revealed that, they have challenged the relationship of the dependents and also the income of the deceased.
The cross examination was also done challenging the manner in which the accident had taken place and question regarding seating capacity alone raised.
This cross examination clearly reveals that the insurance company has not challenged the claim of the claimants to the fact that deceased were travelling in the vehicle as load man.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

The Trial Court in its award has categorically held that based on the averments made in the First Information Report to the effect that the minivan was carrying the milk cans and that the deceased were engaged as a load man for the purpose of loading and unloading the milk cans.
The Trial Court also considered the Insurance Policy - Ex.B4 and recorded that the load men also covered by the policies and premium of Rs.100/- was also collected.
The Registration Certificate of the minivan was marked as Ex.R6 it shows that seating capacity of the minivan is two persons.
Admittedly, 3 persons travelled in the vehicle and two persons who were covered under the policy have made claim for the tortious act of the driver of vehicle in which they had travelled.

13. The Hon'ble Apex Court in United India Insurance Company Limited vs. K. M. Poonam and others (2015) 15 SCC 297, considered the scope for paying compensation for the persons who have travelled in vehicle and having coverage for claiming compensation, though there is violation of seating capacity, has held in paragraph Nos.36 to 39 as follows:
36.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The liability of the insurer, therefore, is confined to the number of persons covered by the insurance https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
17/03/2025 02:14:50 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.959 & 960 of 2022 policy and not beyond the same.

In other words, as in the present case, since the insurance policy of the owner of the vehicle covered six occupants of the vehicle in question, including the driver,
the liability of the insurer would be confined to six persons only, notwithstanding the larger number of persons carried in the vehicle.

Such excess number of persons would have to be treated as third parties, but since no premium had been paid in the policy for them, the insurer would not be liable to make payment of the Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. ... vs Balamani on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122612954/
4 compensation amount as far as they are concerned.

sentences.text: However, the liability of the Insurance Company to make payment even in respect of persons not covered by the insurance policy continues under the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 149 of the Act, as it would be entitled to recover the same if it could prove that one of the conditions of the policy had been breached by the owner of the vehicle.

37. In the instant case, any of the persons travelling in the vehicle in excess of the permitted number of six passengers, though entitled to be compensated by the owner of the vehicle, would still be entitled to receive the compensation amount from the insurer, who could then recover it from the insured owner of the vehicle.

As mentioned hereinbefore, in the instant case, the insurance policy taken out by the owner of the vehicle was in respect of six passengers, including the driver, travelling in the vehicle in question.

The liability for payment of the other passengers in excess of six passengers would be that of the owner of the vehicle who would be required to compensate the injured or the family of the deceased to the extent of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

38. Having arrived at the conclusion that the liability of the Insurance Company to pay compensation was limited to six persons travelling inside the vehicle only and that the liability to pay the others was that of the owner, we, in this case, are faced with the same problem as had surfaced in Anjana Shyam's case.

39. The number of persons to be compensated being in excess of the number of persons who could validly be carried in the vehicle, the question which arises is one of apportionment of the amounts to be paid.

Since there can be no pick and choose method to identify the five passengers, excluding the driver, in respect of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 17/03/2025 02:14:50 pm )
C.M.A.Nos.959 & 960 of 2022 whom compensation would be payable by the Insurance Company, to meet the ends of justice we may apply the procedure adopted in Baljit Kaur's case (supra) and direct that the Insurance Company should deposit the total amount of compensation awarded to all the claimants and the amounts so deposited be disbursed to the claimants in respect to their claims, with liberty to the Insurance Company to recover the amounts paid by it over and above the compensation amounts payable in respect of the persons covered by the Insurance Policy from the owner of the vehicle, as was directed in Baljit Kaur's case.
14. In this case, violation of policy condition is that, the persons travelled in offending vehicle are more than the seating capacity i.e., driver and two load man.
Though, there is violation of policy condition, only two claimants who have coverage, have made claim that they are the load man engaged by the owner of vehicle.

Hence, directing the insurance company to pay the compensation to the claimants would be proper and the insurance company is hereby directed to pay the entire compensation by indemnifying the first respondent/owner of the vehicle, as observed by the Apex Court in Judgment cited supra.
The Tribunal has rightly directed the insurance company to indemnify the first respondent owner of the minivan and considering the nature of violation alleged,

With regard to challenge of the negligence and non impleading the driver and owner of lorry, it is the specific case of the claimants that while the deceased were travelled in the Minivan, the driver of the minivan has not driven it with due diligence and drove the same in high speed and dashed against the lorry.
According to the respondents, the minivan driver has dashed the lorry since the lorry was parked in the middle of the road in negligent manner.
To prove the same, no evidence on the side of the respondents have been produced and without any evidence, respondents deny the negligent of the driver of the minivan.
In the absence of any evidence, the Tribunal has rightly held that driver of minivan, negligently caused the accident.
Under the said circumstances, there is no need for adding or impleading the owner and insurance company of the lorry in this case.
16. Accordingly, both the appeals are dismissed.
